instruction: Display all men's medium-size short-sleeve shirts with a discount of 50% or more.

metadata.explanation: Variation 4: Changed size from L to M, keeps short-sleeve and 50% discount. Maintains same complexity and interaction pattern as original task.

llm_judge_reasons: Critical logic error in Price_discount_range verification (chrome.py:2551): The getter checks that '50_PERCENT_ off & more' is present AND '30_PERCENT_ off & more' is NOT present AND '20_PERCENT_ off & more' is NOT present. This is semantically incorrect.

On e-commerce sites like Macy's, when filtering for '50% or more' discount, the URL often contains multiple discount ranges (e.g., ['50_PERCENT_ off & more', '30_PERCENT_ off & more', '20_PERCENT_ off & more']) because 50% discount includes items with 30% and 20% discounts.

The current logic will FAIL (return 'not_50_PERCENT_ off & more') if the URL contains any other discount percentage filters along with 50%, causing false negatives when the task is actually completed correctly.
The correct logic should check if '50_PERCENT_ off & more' is present in the list, regardless of other discount filters, or verify that 50% is the MINIMUM discount filter selected.
All other aspects of the evaluator are correct: mens_clothing, shirts, Men_regular_size_t, and short_sleeve verification logic is sound.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Fix the Price_discount_range logic in get_macys_product_url_parse (chrome.py:2551): Change from requiring exclusive '50_PERCENT_ off & more' to checking if '50_PERCENT_ off & more' is the highest/only filter, or simply check if '50_PERCENT_ off & more' exists in the list without excluding other filters.
Alternative fix: Check if the discount range list contains ONLY '50_PERCENT_ off & more', or check if it's the most restrictive filter (i.e., the first/primary filter in the list).

Consider the actual Macy's URL structure: Test how the website encodes multiple discount filters and adjust the logic accordingly. The current logic assumes mutual exclusivity which may not match the actual website behavior.
